Upward skip-freeness makes e_k the mean passage time from k to k+1. A nested-set coupling preserves X_t≤Y_t≤X_t+1 for chains started at adjacent levels, so the lower chain reaches k+1 no later than the upper chain reaches k+2; hence e_k is nondecreasing. With u_k=(n-k)α^{k+1}/n and F_k(r)=P_k(K_1≤r), first-step analysis gives u_ke_k=1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r). The same adjacent coupling gives the required tail-sum domination between F_k and F_{k-1}; Abel summation with nondecreasing e_r shows the recurrence numerator is nondecreasing. Therefore (n-k)e_k is nondecreasing and h_0≤e_{n-1}H_n. Kac's return identity at n gives R=1+Σ_{k<n}P_n(K_1=k)h_k, while K_1 is Bin(n,α). Thus A is a convex combination of h_0,…,h_{n-1}, so e_{n-1}=h_{n-1}≤A≤h_0. Combining these inequalities proves A≤h_0≤H_nA. For every fixed η>0, uniformly over η(log n)/n²≤p_n<1, E[T_{n,p_n}]=(1+o(1))A_{n,p_n}=(1+o(1))(R_{n,p_n}-1)/(1-(1-p_n)^n).","claim_sha256":"ea1bda13bba72f45fb6af5237b46ad626f373e6cd3fff9a3caad138672971059","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"The exact first-step recurrence implies e_k/e_{k-1}≥k(1-α^k)/[(n-k)α^{k+1}]. Put m=⌊n/2⌋ and β=m(1-α^m). Uniformly in the claimed range, β≥c_η log n: if mp≤1, then 1-α^m≥mp/2, while if mp>1 it is bounded below by 1-e^{-1}. For a_j=e_{n-j}/e_{n-1} and J=⌊β/2⌋, the ratio bound gives a_{j+1}≤(j/β)a_j for j≤J. Hence Σ_{j=2}^J a_j=O(1/β) and a_J≤β^{-1}2^{-J+2}. Monotonicity of (n-k)e_k then gives a_j≤Ja_J/j for j≥J, whose total tail is at most Ja_J(1+log(n/J))=o(1) uniformly because β≥c_η log n. Consequently h_0/e_{n-1}=1+o(1) uniformly. (iii) If p=c/n with fixed c>0, then n^{-1}log E[T_{n,p}]→I(c):=∫_0^1 log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x)dx>log(1+c). (iv) If np→∞, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼(n²/2)log(1/(1-p)).","claim_sha256":"4070637ecb271f17ade2f83836a619b6a7cdb838c2b713fd4bea53f8263c3db5","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"Writing L=log R, uniformly for p=o(1/n) one has α^{-r}-1=rp+O(r²p²), and summing log(1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1)) gives L=n²p+O(n³p²). At p=γ(log n)/n² this yields R∼n^γ and 1-α^n∼γ(log n)/n, proving (i) via claim 2. In regime (ii), L∼n²p→∞ and |log(np)|=o(n²p), so the denominator does not alter the logarithmic equivalent. For p=c/n, the summands divided by n converge uniformly to the continuous extension of log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x), proving the Riemann-sum limit. Since e^{cx}-1>cx for every x>0, the integrand is strictly greater than log(1+c) on positive measure, establishing the strict inequality. Finally, with ℓ=-log α, exact factorization gives L=[n(n+1)/2]ℓ+nlog n-log(n!)+Σ_r log(1-(1-r/n)e^{-rℓ}). The correction sum has absolute value at most C/ℓ and the factorial term is O(n).
